title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Printing and Distributing the Guiding Opinions on Further Regulating Online Judicial Auction Work
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Further Regulating Online Judicial Auction Work

Fa [2024] No. 238

To: the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Regulating Online Judicial Auction Work are hereby issued. Please conscientiously implement them in light of actual circumstances.

October 29, 2024

Supreme People's Court

Guiding Opinions on Further Regulating Online Judicial Auction Work

To further regulate online judicial auction conduct, focus on improving the level of enforcement asset disposal, and effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties, these opinions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law) and relevant judicial interpretations, taking into account enforcement work practices, with regard to properly conducting online judicial auction work.

1. Conduct thorough investigations into the status of assets. The enforcement court shall investigate the status of assets and may not use "auction as is" as an excuse to avoid investigation duties. For the following assets, the following items shall be the focus of investigation:

(1) For immovable property, investigation shall be conducted by obtaining registration information, site inspections, and door-to-door inquiries, covering information on rights and interests, possession and use, floor plan, transaction tax categories and rates, known defects, and other information.

(2) For motor vehicles, investigation shall be conducted regarding registration information, violation records, emission standards, mileage, and other information significant to the value of the vehicle.

(3) For food products, investigation shall be conducted regarding expiration, spoilage or deterioration, whether they are prohibited for production and sale, and other information, to prevent counterfeit and shoddy food from entering the market through online judicial auctions, thereby endangering the health and safety of the people.

(4) For equity interests, investigation shall be conducted regarding shareholding ratio, subscribed capital, paid-in capital, capital contribution deadlines, financial statements, and dividends, bonuses, and other information significant to the value of the equity interests.

2. Strictly examine the authenticity of rights encumbrances. During the asset investigation process, the enforcement court shall enhance the identification of false rights encumbrances. Where a person not a party to the case claims that a right encumbrance such as a leasehold right or right of habitation exists on the asset, the court shall focus on examining the authenticity of the right encumbrance based on the time of contract signing, lease or habitation term, rent payment, and possession and use. If the facts and assertions raised by the person not a party to the case contradict common life experience or commercial transaction practices, the request of the person not a party to the case for disposal "with leasehold rights" or "with habitation rights" shall not be supported. Where a person not a party to the case has objections, they may seek relief through enforcement objection proceedings. If it is discovered that the judgment debtor and a third party have maliciously colluded to backdate lease contracts, fabricate long-term leases, or otherwise circumvent or obstruct enforcement, legal liability shall be seriously pursued in accordance with the law.

3. Diligently verify the status of construction project costs. When the enforcement court disposes of a construction project, it shall ascertain in accordance with the law whether construction project costs are outstanding, and shall handle the matter separately according to the following circumstances:

(1) If it is discovered that construction project costs are or may be outstanding, but no right holder has made a claim, the enforcement court may, by posting the auction announcement, obtaining the project contract, questioning the judgment debtor, and other means, ascertain the relevant right holder and notify them to promptly assert their rights, in order to resolve the dispute in a single proceeding and minimize subsequent disputes.

(2) Where a person not a party to the case who has not yet obtained an enforcement basis claims a priority right to payment for construction project costs and requests priority payment, the enforcement court shall review the construction project contract and question the judgment debtor. If, upon review, it is determined that the person not a party to the case does not have priority payment rights, and the person not a party to the case disagrees, they may seek relief through enforcement objection proceedings or file a separate lawsuit. If it is determined that the person not a party to the case has priority payment rights, they shall be included in the distribution plan. If a party disagrees with this plan, they may seek relief through the distribution plan objection and distribution plan objection lawsuit procedures.

(3) Where the holder of the priority right to payment for construction project costs claims to have reached an agreement with the judgment debtor for "debt satisfaction through property transfer" and seeks to exclude enforcement on that basis, the enforcement court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 238 of the Civil Procedure Law.

4. Standardize the application of valuation methods. For residential properties and motor vehicles that do not require on-site inspection or appraisal by professionals and for which big data transaction references exist, the online valuation method may be chosen. If a party or interested person believes that the online valuation method should not apply or that the online valuation result clearly deviates from market value, and applies for commissioned appraisal, the enforcement court may approve it upon review.

For immovable property such as industrial plants, construction in progress, land use rights, comprehensive markets with multiple shops, immovable property with high decoration and renovation value, and special or complex assets such as equity interests and mining rights, valuation conditions currently do not exist. If the parties cannot reach an agreement on the price, commissioned appraisal shall apply.

5. Improve the procedures for the conversion of assets involved in criminal cases to monetary value. For enforcement of the property portion of criminal judgments, if the last auction of the assets involved in the case fails, the enforcement court shall, in accordance with the provisions of Article 12, Paragraph 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Enforcement of the Property Portion of Criminal Judgments (Fa Shi [2014] No. 13), seek the opinions of the financial department and the victim regarding whether they agree to accept the assets or accept property as restitution. If the financial department and the victim do not agree to accept the assets or property as restitution, an auction without a reserve price may be conducted. However, for the auction without a reserve price of assets of high value such as immovable property, mining rights, and large blocks of stocks, the deposit and bid increment shall be reasonably determined, and subject to deliberation by the collegial panel and approval by the presiding leader of the court.

6. Truthfully disclose information on auctioned assets. The enforcement court shall comprehensively and truthfully disclose the status, possession and use, known defects, and rights encumbrances of the auctioned assets as ascertained during the property investigation. Concealing or exaggerating defects in the auctioned assets is strictly prohibited.

If the auctioned asset is immovable property, the enforcement court shall disclose the possession and use status of the immovable property in the auction announcement. Expressions such as "possession unknown" or "occupied by others" shall not be used in the auction announcement. If a decision is made to auction "with leasehold rights" or "with habitation rights", important information such as possession and use status, rent, term, and details of the relevant rights holders shall be truthfully disclosed.

If laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations impose restrictions on the bidding qualifications of buyers, such restrictions shall be announced in the auction announcement.

7. Improve the mechanism for self-disposal by the judgment debtor. If a second online judicial auction fails, and the creditor applies for taking assets in lieu of payment or a third party applies for purchasing at the failed auction price, the enforcement court shall notify the judgment debtor. If the judgment debtor claims to self-dispose of the auctioned asset at a price higher than the failed auction price, the enforcement court may allow it upon review, and the procedures for taking assets in lieu of payment or third-party purchase shall be temporarily suspended.

The self-disposal period shall be determined by the enforcement court based on the condition of the asset, market conditions, and other factors, and shall generally not exceed 60 days. If the self-disposal of immovable property is successful, after the buyer pays the full price to the enforcement court, the enforcement court may issue a ruling on the transfer of ownership for the transaction. If the buyer pays part of the price and the remaining part is financed through loans or other means, and the buyer submits relevant financing procedures to the enforcement court, the enforcement court may, after coordinating with the immovable property registration authority and obtaining its consent, issue a ruling on the transfer of ownership for the transaction, and the buyer and seller may go through the "transfer with seal" procedures. If the judgment debtor fails in the self-disposal, the enforcement court shall initiate procedures for taking assets in lieu of payment, third-party purchase, and other procedures.

8. Step up the delivery of immovable properties after vacation. When disposing of immovable property, unless there are legal grounds, the enforcement court shall be responsible for the delivery after vacation, and it is strictly prohibited to declare in the auction announcement that "the court is not responsible for vacation".

If delivery after vacation needs to be organized, the enforcement court shall formulate a vacation plan, actively urge the judgment debtor and other occupants to vacate voluntarily. If they still do not vacate voluntarily after being urged, the court shall strictly enforce the vacation in accordance with the law, and ensure the recording of law enforcement, safety guarantees, and other work.

If, during the vacation process, the judgment debtor or a person not a party to the case engages in acts such as damaging the property or obstructing enforcement, they shall be subject to fines or detention depending on the severity of the act. If the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law.

9. Strictly apply collegial deliberation and approval for major matters. The enforcement court shall establish a list of powers and records for major matters. Important matters such as the starting price, bid increment, rights encumbrances, auction of the sole residential property, self-disposal, taking assets in lieu of payment, and third-party purchase at the failed auction price shall be subject to collegial deliberation, reported for approval in accordance with procedures, and strictly subject to the review and approval system of the bureau (division) head. No single enforcement officer may make such decisions alone.

10. Strengthen the management of auction support work. All high and intermediate people's courts shall strengthen unified management of auction support work within their jurisdiction and increase guidance on auction support work for major, complex, and sensitive cases. Intermediate people's courts with the necessary conditions may, based on the actual circumstances of their jurisdiction, set up relatively fixed personnel or teams to be uniformly responsible for auction support work within the jurisdiction. If the enforcement court entrusts auction support work to an auction support institution, it shall strengthen supervision over the performance of duties by the auction support institution, and it is strictly prohibited to entrust matters that must be handled by enforcement personnel in accordance with laws and judicial interpretations to auction support institutions. It is strictly prohibited for auction support personnel to use the case handling system, accounts, and keys, to prevent leaks of case handling secrets. It is strictly prohibited to privately contact bidders. If on-site viewing is needed, at least two auction support personnel must be present. It is strictly prohibited for auction support institutions, auction support personnel, and their close relatives to participate in the bidding for assets for which they provide auction support work. It is strictly prohibited to disclose information on potential bidders to third parties. It is strictly prohibited to illegally collect fees to improperly exclude potential bidders. Effective management measures shall be formulated in light of the work realities of the jurisdiction, clearly defining the work responsibilities and checklists of auction support institutions, standardizing fee calculation methods and standards, and strictly regulating the access and exit procedures of auction support institutions. A mechanism for investigating disciplinary and illegal conduct shall be established. If an auction support institution is found to have engaged in illegal or non-compliant conduct or no longer meets the requirements for being included in the database, disciplinary measures such as suspension, cancellation of entrustment qualifications, or even expulsion shall be imposed depending on the severity of the circumstances.

11. Crack down on acts disrupting the online judicial auction order in accordance with the law. For acts that seriously disrupt the online judicial auction order, such as promoting one-stop services such as "pre-auction investigation", "property clearance and takeover", and "liaison with the court" through exaggerating, concealing, or misleading means, inducing bidders to pay high commissions, or even forging judicial documents to defraud property, people's courts at all levels shall actively cooperate with public security, housing and urban-rural construction, market supervision and management, and other departments to resolutely crack down in accordance with the law. A regular working mechanism shall be established to safeguard the order of online judicial auctions in accordance with the law, by intensifying publicity on online judicial auctions, regularly publishing typical cases, and carrying out special activities.

12. Deepen comprehensive supervision of online judicial auctions. People's courts at all levels shall strictly carry out work in accordance with laws and judicial interpretations to ensure that online judicial auctions are open, transparent, timely, efficient, and fully documented. They shall actively accept the full-course supervision of the auction activities by the parties and the public. Issues concerning the auction raised by the parties, the public, or the media shall be promptly verified, corrected, and addressed in response to public concerns.

They shall actively accept legal supervision by the procuratorial authorities, promote information sharing, and smooth supervision channels, so as to make procuratorial supervision of enforcement standardized, regular, and institutionalized. For cases involving auctions or post-vacation deliveries that are major, sensitive, complex, or have sparked strong public concern, the procuratorial authorities may be invited to be present to supervise the enforcement activities.
